Expectation1: Look out for each other's safety and well-being
Situation1: The siblings are walking home from school together on a familiar street.
Expectation2: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation2: A friend sends a text message complaining about having a long, boring day.
Story: As my little brother and I walked home from school, I kept an eye on him like Mom always asked. He was skipping ahead, humming, and I felt that familiar tug of responsibility—make sure he’s safe, don’t let him wander too far. My phone buzzed in my pocket. It was Mia, my best friend. “Ugh, today was the worst. Can you talk?” she wrote. I knew she needed me; she always said I was the only one who really listened. I wanted to be there for her, to reply right away and let her vent. But my brother was already halfway down the block, and I had to keep up, make sure he didn’t dart into the street or get distracted. My fingers hovered over my phone, torn between texting Mia back and focusing on my brother. I could feel the pressure building—Mia counting on me for support, my brother counting on me for safety. I wished I could split myself in two, but I couldn’t. I hesitated, heart pounding, caught between being the sibling I was supposed to be and the friend I wanted to be.
